submission.justification: Module-D1 has the highest light yield on paper (38 PE/MeV at 20% in the 2025 summary), but its thin bonded light guide fails 30% of modules after 20 thermal cycles, far above the 5% hard limit, and failed modules cannot be replaced. Module-D2 passes thermal cycling (0.5%) but gives only ~23.9 PE/MeV at 30% coverage. Module-D3 passes thermal cycling (2% failed, from the test batch) and gives 37.0 PE/MeV at 30% coverage in the Geant4 simulation, the highest light collection among the compliant designs. 30% is the top of the allowed coverage range, and the meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs exist for 30% coverage. Light yield rises with coverage, so 30% is the best choice within constraints.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three candidate designs
requirements.evidence: Module-D3 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) from candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules fail after 20 thermal cycles (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: query_thermal_cycling returned 2.0% failed for Module-D3; thermal_cycling_tests.md reports 2% from a 40-module batch
Coverage set to 30%, the upper bound of the allowed range
Simulated 37.0 PE/MeV for D3 at 30% vs 23.9 for D2 at 30%. D1 is higher on paper but fails the thermal constraint, so it is excluded. Light yield for D3 at 30% is the best among compliant options.
